mphl.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
mphl.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match).

mphl.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
mphl.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

mphl.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
mphl.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred.

mphl.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mphl.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms.

mphl.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mphl.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use.

mphl.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mphl.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'.

mphl.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.
mphl.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

odt.context: A submerged or free-flowing opening through which water discharges under head. Appears in Orifice Flow and Orifice Drain Time calculators.
odt.translation_notes: In irrigation contexts, often the opening of a headgate or pipe turnout. Use the hydraulic engineering term, not a general word for 'hole' or 'opening'.

odt.context: Coefficient correcting theoretical orifice or weir flow for real-world contraction and friction effects. Appears in Orifice and Weir calculators.
odt.translation_notes: The 'discharge' here refers to flow rate, not the verb. Use the hydraulic engineering compound term.

odt.context: Water surface elevation on the upstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Weir Flow and Orifice calculators.
odt.translation_notes: 'Headwater' is an upstream water surface — do not confuse with 'head' (energy) or 'source' (origin of a stream). Use the hydraulic structure term.

odt.context: Water surface elevation on the downstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Orifice Flow calculator. When tailwater is above the invert, the orifice is submerged.
odt.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic structure term for downstream water level. Pair consistently with 'headwater elevation'.

Tempo di svuotamento = t(H<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>1</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>) − t(H<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>2</sub>,A<sub>0</sub>), dove H<sub>1</sub> = quota iniziale − quota orifizio, H<sub>2</sub> = quota finale − quota orifizio.
